_about: In His Steps: the Christian edition, for daily quiet times. Same app as Well Lived,
with its own name, welcome page, quotes, colours and voices. The library of quotable
works is sources.json in this folder (made by tools/make_christian_sources.py), and
Claude's instructions are in prompts/. Run it with EDITION=christian.
description: A private journal for your daily quiet time, with a reflection from Scripture after every entry.
lead: A quiet place to reflect each day and draw on Christian wisdom.

points.title: Build a daily habit of quiet time
points.text: A few minutes of honest writing each day. Your streak keeps count, and a prompt is there when the page feels blank.

points.title: Rooted in Scripture and the great devotional writers
points.text: Reflections draw from the Gospels, Paul’s letters, and the Psalms, alongside classic voices like Augustine, Luther, Calvin, Bunyan, Edwards, and Spurgeon, with links to the original texts.

points.title: Grow in His Steps
points.text: Every reflection ends with an honest question to carry through your day. Browse back by date, or keep favourites close.

points.title: A fully private, encrypted journal
points.text: Entries are locked with a passphrase only you know. Download your whole journal at any time.

welcome_quote.text: “Search me, God, and know my heart; test me and know my anxious thoughts.”

sources_intro: Reflections quote only the works below. Every quotation is checked word for word against the text before you see it, and links to the passage it came from; if it can't be confirmed, the reflection puts the idea in its own words instead. Scripture is from the Berean Standard Bible (BSB), a modern translation from the Hebrew and Greek, dedicated to the public domain in 2023. The other writers are in public-domain editions from the Christian Classics Ethereal Library (CCEL), Project Gutenberg and Wikisource.

source_groups.name: Old Testament
source_groups.about: The Psalms for prayer in every mood, the wisdom of Proverbs and Ecclesiastes, and Isaiah's comfort.

source_groups.name: The Gospels
source_groups.about: The life and teaching of Jesus, including the Sermon on the Mount and the parables.

source_groups.name: Paul's letters
source_groups.about: Grace, freedom and the new life in Christ, above all in Romans, Galatians, Ephesians and Philippians.

source_groups.name: Hebrews and the general letters
source_groups.about: Faith that endures and faith that works: Hebrews, James, Peter and John.

source_groups.name: The early and medieval church
source_groups.about: Augustine's restless heart and Aquinas on grace and the virtues.

source_groups.name: Devotional classics
source_groups.about: Two Catholic classics long treasured by Protestants: following Christ in humility, and practising God's presence in ordinary work.

source_groups.name: The Reformation
source_groups.about: Freedom by faith alone, and the shape of the Christian life.

source_groups.name: The Puritans
source_groups.about: Searching the heart, fighting sin by the Spirit, and the pilgrim road.

source_groups.name: Revival and the evangelical tradition
source_groups.about: From the Great Awakening to the 20th century: true religion, daily devotion, holiness, humility and hunger for God.

paraphrase_only.about: These writers are still in copyright, so reflections may draw on their ideas in their own words, naming the writer and book, but never quote them, and there are no links.
